brief: A small-parts organizer with at least six separate bins.

requirements.evidence: Six half-depth bins in a compact hex cluster, sized for small parts. M3 screw, nut and standoff piles show what it's for; all six are visible from above.
Six separate bins, one per base: bin:0,0,0, bin:-1,0,0, bin:-1,1,0, bin:0,-1,0, bin:1,-1,0 and bin:1,0,0.

finish.summary: I built a small-parts organizer with six separate bins. Six full hex bases are joined in a compact cluster, and each one holds its own half-depth bin (hex-bin-half). I ran the two house rules: solid end caps went on every open outer face, and joint bolts lock the bases together. That makes 30 parts in all, and the print estimate is about 2649 g of filament. For display only, each bin has a pile of M3 screws, nuts or standoffs. These sit below the bin rims, so they're easy to see from above but hidden from the side. check_build passed with no issues and the mesh-collision check reads clear.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
